title: Caring for wool crochet
subtitle: How to wash, dry, and store crochet made from wool without felting or distorting it
excerpt: Wool can felt irreversibly if washed at the wrong temperature or agitated too hard. Handled correctly it lasts years; handled carelessly it turns into stiff, shrunken fabric.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book. Pauline Turner, How to Crochet (HarperCollins).

glossaryTerms.definition: The irreversible matting of wool fibres caused by heat, moisture, and agitation together. The fabric shrinks and loses all stitch definition.
Wool that has been chemically or mechanically treated to remove or flatten the scales on the fibre, making it machine-washable without felting.

content.text: Wool fibres have microscopic scales that lock together under heat and agitation, causing
is treated to prevent this and can usually be machine-washed. Untreated wool must be washed by hand in cool water with minimal agitation. Check the ball band before washing to confirm the treatment.
Fill a basin with cool water (30 degrees C or below) and a small amount of wool wash or mild soap.
Submerge the piece and gently press it through the water. Do not rub, wring, or scrub.
Let soak for 10 minutes. Drain and gently press out water. Do not lift the piece by one end; support the whole weight.
Refill with clean cool water at the same temperature and press through once to rinse. Changing temperature during the wash cycle can shock-felt the fibres.
Roll in a clean towel and press to remove water. Do not wring.
Lay flat to dry on a towel or blocking mat, reshaped to measurements. Do not hang to dry; wet wool stretches under its own weight.

Superwash wool can usually be machine-washed on a delicate or wool cycle in cool water. Use a mesh laundry bag to prevent the piece catching on the drum. Still lay flat to dry rather than tumble drying.

Store wool crochet clean, folded (not hung), in a breathable bag or drawer. Moths are attracted to soiled wool more than clean wool. Cedarwood or lavender sachets deter moths. Do not use sealed plastic bags; wool needs airflow.

items.symptom: The piece has shrunk and the stitches are no longer visible
items.cause: The wool felted due to heat, agitation, or a temperature change during washing.
items.fix: Felting is not reversible. For untreated wool, hand-wash at a consistent cool temperature with minimal movement. Check the ball band next time to confirm whether the yarn is superwash.

items.symptom: The piece stretched out of shape after washing
items.cause: It was hung to dry while wet.
items.fix: Wet wool stretches under its own weight. Lay flat to dry, patting back to the original measurements while still damp.

content.text: After washing and blocking a wool piece, measure it against the pre-wash measurements. Most wool pieces come out within a centimetre of the blocked measurements. If the piece grew significantly, the yarn may be unsuperwashed wool that needs more careful handling.
